_note: Module names are inferred from the timetable (session lead, room, session type) because Aston does not publish the code meanings. 'confidence' says how sure the inference is. Every module page must show a small 'Names inferred — check against your module handbook' note until Ari confirms it via the edit button.

themes.Management: Clinical management: dispensing, refraction, contact lenses, binocular vision, paediatrics
themes.Patient: Examining the patient: anterior eye, posterior eye, diagnosis

modules.name: Refraction & Management of Refractive Error
outline: Subjective refraction: best vision sphere, fogging, duochrome
Binocular balancing (Humphriss immediate contrast, prism dissociation)
Presbyopia and near add determination (age guide, plus-build-up, range of clear vision)
Prescribing decisions: when to change, partial prescribing, anisometropia
Presbyope clinic: running a full refraction on a real presbyopic patient

modules.name: Contact Lenses
outline: Keratometry and corneal topography for lens selection
Soft lens materials: hydrogel vs silicone hydrogel, water content, Dk and Dk/t
Soft lens fitting assessment: centration, movement, push-up test, coverage
RGP fitting and fluorescein patterns (alignment, steep, flat)
Choosing lens power: vertex distance correction above ±4.00 D
Care regimes, hygiene and patient instruction (insertion, removal)
Aftercare and complications: CLPU, CLARE, microbial keratitis, neovascularisation, GPC
Grading scales (Efron / CCLRU) and recording findings

modules.name: Anterior Eye Examination
outline: Slit lamp illumination techniques: diffuse, direct focal, parallelepiped, optic section, specular, retro-illumination, sclerotic scatter
Systematic anterior segment examination: lids, lashes, conjunctiva, cornea, AC, iris, lens
Van Herick anterior chamber angle grading
Fluorescein and lissamine green staining; grading corneal staining
Tear film assessment: TBUT, NIBUT, tear meniscus, Schirmer
Common conditions: blepharitis, MGD, dry eye, conjunctivitis types

modules.name: Posterior Eye (and Glaucoma)
outline: Indirect fundus examination with slit lamp and Volk lens
Optic disc assessment: size, cup-to-disc ratio, neuroretinal rim, ISNT rule
Macula and retinal vessels: what normal looks like
Glaucoma risk factors and referral criteria (check NICE / College guidance)

modules.name: Diagnosis & Systemic Disease
outline: Interpreting clinical data in PC-lab cases

modules.name: Paediatrics
outline: Assessing vision in children (preferential looking, Kay pictures, Cardiff cards)

modules.name: Vision Science & Evidence
outline: Using the library and literature search

modules.name: Duty of Candour
outline: What the professional duty of candour requires
Apologising and explaining when things go wrong

modules.name: Public Health & Eye Health
outline: Causes of sight loss in the UK
Health inequalities and access to eye care
